name: Skärvik Fishing Village
region: Northern Bohuslän, on the Skagerrak coast
description: Skärvik clings to a cleft in the bare granite of the Bohuslän coast, its white and red houses crowded together on rock ledges above a narrow harbour. The great herring shoals that made the coast rich left sixty years ago and have not returned; the people fish for cod, ling, mackerel and lobster, farm thin patches of soil between the rocks, and look out to sea. Beyond the village lies treeless heath and skerries without number.
seasonNotes: August, late summer. The lobster season opens and the boats go out at dawn with the creels. The water is at its warmest and the evenings are long and golden, though the first dark nights return at the month's end. The heath is purple with heather. Hay is drying in small fields between the rocks, and the women split and salt fish on the jetties. Squalls come in from the west without warning.
travel: From Uppsala by rail to Gothenburg via Stockholm and the western line, about a day and a half, then by coastal steamer north along the skerries, a further day.
publicFacts: The herring has not returned to the Bohuslän coast since 1808; old men still keep the salting houses in hope.
Last autumn a boat with four men from Skärvik was lost in a storm off the outer skerries; their widows receive a small parish relief.
The coastal steamer calls at Skärvik twice a week in summer and not at all when the ice comes.
Several young men have shipped out as sailors on Norwegian ships, and a few have stayed in America.
The vicar serves three island parishes and travels between them by boat.
Fishermen and farmers disagree over the rights to collect seaweed for fertiliser on the shore.
A pilot lives on the island beyond the harbour and guides ships through the skerries.

places.name: The Harbour Cottages
places.ownerRole: the fishermen's families; the eldest fisherman speaks for them
places.description: Small fishermen's cottages huddle on the rock above the harbour, each with its boathouse below and nets hanging to dry on poles. Children jump into the cold water from the jetty. The smell of tar, fish and seaweed is everywhere. Gulls scream over the gutting tables, where the women work fast with short knives.

affordances.name: Cottage room
affordances.description: One room: hearth, a box bed for the parents, a pull-out bench for the children, a table under the window.

affordances.name: Well

affordances.name: Potato patch
affordances.description: A tiny garden of potatoes in soil carried up in baskets, walled against the wind.

places.name: Bergsgården
places.ownerRole: a farming and fishing family, freeholders of Bergsgården
places.description: The only real farm in Skärvik lies inland in a hollow of the heath where enough soil has gathered for fields. Low stone walls divide the small pastures, and the house is painted white with a slate roof weighted with stones. Sheep graze among the heather and juniper. From the hill behind, you can see the whole sea and the line of the skerries.

affordances.name: Farmyard
affordances.description: The yard between the buildings, trodden mud and a woodpile.

affordances.name: Main room
affordances.description: The everyday room: open hearth, long table, wall beds and the loom in the corner.

contains.name: Open hearth
contains.description: The whitewashed corner hearth with its iron pot-hook.

affordances.name: Best room
affordances.description: The cold best room, painted furniture, the family Bible and a clock from Mora.

contains.name: Dowry chest
contains.description: A painted chest with the wife's linen and the year of her wedding on the lid.

affordances.name: Farmhands' chamber
affordances.description: A bare chamber with two beds and the hands' own chests.

affordances.name: Cowshed
affordances.description: A low dark byre, warm with cattle breath.

affordances.name: Stable
affordances.description: A stable for the farm horse or horses.

affordances.name: Barn
affordances.description: A timber barn for the harvest.

contains.name: Hayloft
contains.description: The hay store over the barn floor, reached by a ladder.

affordances.name: Threshing barn
affordances.description: A threshing barn (loge) where the grain is threshed with flails through the autumn.

affordances.name: Root cellar
affordances.description: A root cellar dug into the slope, holding potatoes, turnips and the milk.

affordances.name: Well
affordances.description: A well with a sweep pole and a wooden bucket.

affordances.name: Bathhouse
affordances.description: A small log bastu with a stone oven, also used for drying malt and flax.

places.name: Skärvik Church
places.description: The church stands on a bare rock above the village, white walls blinding in the sun, a landmark for boats coming home. The graves are cut into thin soil among the rocks, and many stones remember men lost at sea. Inside, a model ship hangs from the ceiling, given by sailors after a rescue. The wind never stops whistling through the bell tower.

affordances.name: Sacristy
affordances.description: A small vaulted room off the chancel where the vicar robes.

contains.name: Vestment cupboard
contains.description: A tall cupboard of chasubles, the surplice and spare altar candles.

contains.name: Parish chest
contains.description: An ancient iron-banded chest with three locks for the communion silver and old deeds.

affordances.name: Bell tower
affordances.description: Steep ladders up to the bells, bird droppings on the beams, wind through the louvres.

affordances.name: Church loft
affordances.description: The dusty space above the vaults, full of broken pews and old hatchments.

places.name: The Parsonage
places.ownerRole: the vicar of the parish, who lives here and serves the church
places.description: The parsonage is a solid house sheltered behind the church hill, with a walled garden that is the only green trees in the village. The vicar's boat is pulled up on the slip below. Roses grow against the south wall in defiance of the salt wind. Inside, the study is lined with books and smells of pipe smoke and sea damp.

affordances.name: Vicar's study
affordances.description: The study where the vicar writes sermons and receives parishioners.

contains.name: Vicar's desk
contains.description: A desk under the window with sermon drafts.

contains.name: Locked drawer
contains.description: A locked drawer for private letters and certificates waiting to be signed.

contains.name: Bookshelves
contains.description: Shelves of postils, Luther, hymnals and back numbers of church journals.

affordances.name: Parish registers
affordances.description: The church books: household examination rolls, birth, death and moving registers.

affordances.name: Parlour
affordances.description: The parsonage parlour where the vicar's wife receives.

affordances.name: Kitchen
affordances.description: The parsonage kitchen.

affordances.name: Glebe barn
affordances.description: The barn of the glebe farm.

affordances.name: Glebe cowshed
affordances.description: The parsonage cowshed.

affordances.name: Parsonage garden
affordances.description: An orchard and kitchen garden, the vicar's pride.

places.name: The Harbour Inn
places.ownerRole: the keeper of the Harbour Inn
places.description: The inn is a big old house at the harbour that was once a herring merchant's salting house, now with rooms for passengers waiting for the steamer. The taproom has a view of the boats through small windows and a stove for cold evenings. Fishermen gather in the evening to argue about the weather. The floor is scattered with sand and smells of the sea.

affordances.name: Taproom
affordances.description: The public room: benches, a long scrubbed table, a tiled stove and the day's travellers.

affordances.name: Kitchen
affordances.description: A smoky kitchen with an open hearth, copper pans and a bread rack under the ceiling.

contains.name: Pantry
contains.description: A cold larder of salted meat, cheeses, crispbread and the brännvin keg.

places.name: The Boat Smithy
places.description: A small stone smithy by the slipway makes anchors, boat nails and hooks. The smith also repairs the iron rings on the jetty and the moorings. The open door looks out over the bright water. Rust and tar mix with the smell of the forge.

affordances.name: Forge
affordances.description: The hearth and bellows, the anvil on its stump, the quench trough.

affordances.name: Workshop
affordances.description: The bench and racks of tongs, hammers and half-finished work.

affordances.name: Coal shed
affordances.description: A shed of charcoal and bar iron from the works.

affordances.name: Smith's cottage

contains.name: Smith's chest
contains.description: The smith's own chest of papers and good clothes.

places.name: The Cottage on the Heath
places.ownerRole: the wise woman on the heath
places.description: An old woman's cottage stands alone on the open heath, sheltered by a single twisted rowan. Heather and wild thyme grow right up to the walls, and a few sheep wander round it. Seaweed and herbs dry on the rocks in the sun. From the door you can see both the village below and the sea beyond.

affordances.name: Cottage room
affordances.description: A single low room, dim and smelling of smoke and herbs.

contains.name: Hearth
contains.description: A hearth with a brew always going.

affordances.name: Herb store
affordances.description: Bunches of drying herbs from the rafters, jars of salve and dried roots.
